body: Quick pass: mergeable with main, body complete, quick and batch gates green at 4ae6a9ed, and the issue isn't paused. Flagging ready. **A note for the reviewer:** the 8 in vise's default maximum opening (8.25 in) is smaller than the 6 in's (9 in). It came from the issue's single catalog figure, and many 8 in vises open wider. Please check whether the default should be raised from public spec sheets. Users can edit it, so it's not a blocker.

Decision from the user (2026-11-11): **the standard size table is fine as it stands**, including the 8 in figures. Any vise can be customised through the editable dimensions this PR ships, so the reviewer doesn't need to re-research the 8 in maximum opening.

Back to draft: the review found one blocker. The vise row's jaw-opening draft is a single slot, so with two built-in vises the field can't be edited and Set lands the old value. Details are in the review comment. Flag it ready again once the fix is pushed and gated.

Review findings fixed in c2a3f873 (`fix(ui,app): per-vise opening drafts; jaw body depth; review pins`). The PR stays a draft.

**Blocker: two vise rows shared one opening draft.**
- `State::vise_opening` is now a map keyed by vise name (`HashMap<String, ViseOpeningDraft { live, value }>`), read through `State::vise_opening_draft(name, live) -> &mut f64`. Each row keeps its own draft.
- A draft refreshes from the live opening whenever that changes (Set, Open to stock, undo, redo), so the field never shows a stale value after an undo (review note 2).
- `State::retire_vise_opening_drafts()` runs at the top of the Fixtures page and drops the draft of any vise that was deleted, renamed or is no longer a vise.
- Pin: `fixture_vise_tests::two_vise_rows_keep_their_own_opening_drafts`. It places two 6 in vises, types 90 into the first row's field through kittest, runs a frame, then clicks the first Set opening. The first vise ends at 90 and the second is untouched. Deleting the first vise retires its draft and leaves the second's. **Before the fix it failed:** `left: Some(114.3) right: Some(90.0)`, the same failure the review reproduced. It passes after the fix.
- Also pinned: `a_vise_row_sets_its_opening_and_opens_to_the_stock` now checks that the field follows an undo.

**Thin jaws: a new `jaw_body_depth` parameter.**
- This is the plate plus the steel behind it, at least the jaw thickness (refused by name when less). It extends each jaw's solid back along the screw, up to jaw height.
- Default: 2 x the jaw thickness on every row (`vise::table::BODY_PER_PLATE`). Every row still has room at the max opening; the tightest is 160 mm, with 28 mm to spare.
- It can be edited in the dialog, over MCP (`jaw_body_depth` dimension) and in the file. A file saved without it reads it as 2 x the thickness.
- The reasoning is recorded in `docs/decisions/788-builtin-vises.md`.
- Pin: `builtin_vise::steel_behind_a_jaw_plate_below_jaw_height_is_struck`. On every size, a point behind either jaw plate below jaw height is inside the solid, and a 4 mm tool crossing there is struck (`FixtureMesh::band_meets`). **It failed before the fix** and passes after.
- The shell, volume and bounds pins now use the body depth. There are new refusal pins for a body shallower than the plate and for a NaN depth.

**Missing pins (both pass; they pin behaviour that was already correct):**
- `builtin_vise::undoing_set_vise_restores_the_old_facets`: undo returns the exact old facets, and redo the new ones.
- `builtin_vise::a_nonsense_vise_key_is_dropped_on_load_logged_and_the_steel_kept`: a saved vise key spoiled to an over-max opening still loads. The fixture and its facets stay, `vise` is `None`, and the warning "vise parameters dropped on load … over the max opening" is captured. `SetVise` then refuses it as "not a built-in vise".

**Gate (head c2a3f873)**
| What | Result |
|---|---|
| app `builtin_vise` / `mcp_vise` / `fixtures` / `fixture_mesh` | 9 / 1 / 14 / 3 passed |
| app `fixture_ux` / `fixture_library` / `project_roundtrip` / `commands_undo` | 9 / 6 / 71 / 32 passed |
| ui `--lib` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 460 passed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| Linux quick gate (`--base upstream/main`) | app suites ok, ui suites ok, 0 failed |

No snapshot PNGs or process files changed.
